title: Pineapple Upside-Down Cake
description: Sticky, caramelised pineapple upside-down cake. Built from pantry staples, baked in a water tray for a moist, even crumb, flipped warm, and it didn't stick. Looks awesome. Tastes even better.

ingredients.notes: divided: 45ml for Caramel Topping, 120ml for Cake Batter

youWillNeed.note: for the water bath — filled with 2–3 cm boiling water
wider than the tin for the flip

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Grease a 20 cm round cake tin well and line the base with baking paper.
Place a deep roasting tray on the bottom rack of the oven and fill with 2–3 cm of boiling water. This is your steam tray — it stays in the oven the whole time.
In a small bowl, mix 90 g brown sugar with 45 ml of the pineapple juice until a thick paste forms. Spread evenly across the base of the tin.
Pat the pineapple rings dry with paper towel, then arrange them on top of the caramel paste in a single layer.
In a large bowl, whisk together 160 g white sugar, 110 ml vegetable oil, and the eggs until pale and slightly thickened — about 2 minutes.
Sift in 200 g plain flour, 10 g baking powder, and 2 g salt. Fold gently until just combined.
Pour in the remaining 120 ml of pineapple juice and fold through until the batter is smooth and uniform. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter over the pineapple topping and spread level with a spatula.
Place the cake tin on the middle rack, directly above the water tray. Bake for 40–45 minutes until deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Remove from oven and rest in the tin for exactly 5 minutes — no more. This is the window: too soon and it falls apart, too late and the caramel sets and glues to the tin.
Run a thin knife around the edge of the tin. Place a serving plate face-down over the tin, hold both firmly, and flip in one confident motion.
Lift the tin straight up. If any fruit sticks, peel it off and press it back into place. Cool for 15 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

notes.title: The 5-Minute Flip Window
notes.content: 5 minutes out of the oven is non-negotiable. Too soon — the batter hasn't set fully and the cake splits. Too late — the caramel cools, hardens, and welds the fruit to the tin. Set a timer.

notes.title: Why Plain Flour + Baking Powder
notes.content: Self-raising flour has baking powder baked in at a fixed ratio you can't control. Using plain flour and measured baking powder (10 g per 200 g flour) gives consistent lift every time. No bi-carb needed — there's no strong acid in the batter to activate it.

notes.title: Water Tray in the Oven
notes.content: A tray of boiling water on the bottom rack creates steam throughout the bake. This keeps the crumb moist and tender, slows the top from over-browning, and prevents the surface from cracking. It's a small step that makes a noticeable difference.

notes.title: Caramel Without Butter
notes.content: Brown sugar dissolved in pineapple juice forms a sticky, glossy caramel topping with no dairy required. Patting the rings dry first stops the caramel from watering down and ensures good colour.

notes.title: Serving
notes.content: Best served warm, about 15 minutes after flipping. A spoonful of thickened cream or vanilla ice cream alongside is not optional.

notes.title: Storage
notes.content: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Best within 24 hours. Reheat individual slices in the microwave for 10–12 seconds to restore the sticky caramel texture.

journal.content: Made with 86 g brown sugar and 150 ml pineapple juice at the time. Used a water basin — added 10 minutes to bake time. Flipped at exactly 5 minutes. Didn't stick. Looked awesome. Dish pig survived.
